economy.summary: His campaign site says he supports policies that back the industries driving the rural economy, including agriculture, forestry, and the oil and gas industries, and advocates expanding broadband service to the region.
economy.short: Supports agriculture, forestry, oil and gas; backs broadband expansion.

taxes.summary: Voted for the $50.8 billion 2026-27 state budget, saying the General Assembly significantly reduced the governor's proposed spending without tapping the Rainy Day Fund and that the plan includes no new or increased taxes for families or employers.
taxes.short: Voted for 2026-27 budget; says reduced spending, no new taxes.

abortion.summary: Voted in December 2025 against House Bill 1957, a proposed amendment to the Pennsylvania Constitution providing for personal reproductive liberty, which passed the House 102-101; his campaign site separately says he fights for the right to life.
abortion.short: Voted against reproductive-liberty constitutional amendment; cites right to life.

education.summary: His campaign site says he fights for schools and advocates funding for rural schools; it does not detail further education policy.
education.short: Advocates funding for rural schools; no further detail.

healthcare.summary: His official legislative page describes him as an advocate for rural health care and emergency medical services and says he twice authored legislation to increase Medicaid reimbursement for ambulance services.
healthcare.short: Advocates rural health care; authored ambulance Medicaid reimbursement increases.

energy.summary: As Republican chairman of the House energy committee, he joined in unveiling a 10-bill package that the caucus says would increase energy production, lower electricity costs, and strengthen grid reliability through an all-of-the-above energy strategy; he also announces natural gas impact fee revenue for the district.
energy.short: Backs 10-bill package to increase production, lower electricity costs.

guns.summary: His campaign site says he fights to defend Second Amendment rights and opposed efforts to take those rights away.
guns.short: Says he defends Second Amendment rights.

healthcare.summary: His campaign site says access to health care should not depend on your ZIP code and pledges to fight for policies that protect and expand rural health care access and support local hospitals and providers.
healthcare.short: Pledges to protect and expand rural health care access.

energy.summary: Opposes new data center projects in the region, saying they strain local energy, water, land, and infrastructure while creating few local jobs; his site does not detail a broader energy platform.
energy.short: Opposes new data centers, citing strain on energy, water, infrastructure.

guns.summary: On public safety, his campaign site opposes mass surveillance systems that monitor people without clear limits, accountability, or public oversight, and supports transparency and strict privacy protections before surveillance technology is adopted; the site does not state a position on guns.
guns.short: Opposes mass surveillance; supports privacy protections; no guns position.
